**(iv) Reaction with Reactive Metals:** An Acid undergoes a reaction with reactive metals (\text{K}, \text{Na}, \text{Mg} etc.) and produces salts of that metal and hydrogen as well. For example, $\text{Mg}$ undergoes a reaction with sulfuric acid and produces $\text{MgSO}_4$ and $\text{H}_2$ gas.
$$\text{Mg} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{MgSO}_4 + \text{H}_2 \uparrow$$

**(v) Reaction between Dilute Acid and Metallic Carbonate:** Dilute acids undergo reactions with metallic carbonate to produce salt, water and carbon dioxide. For example, calcium carbonate and dilute $\text{HCl}$ undergo a reaction and produce calcium chloride salt, water and carbon dioxide gas. The gas comes out in bubbles.
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \longrightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2 \uparrow$$

Channel this produced carbon dioxide in lime water, the lime water will turn turbid. The reaction is:
$$\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{CO}_2 \longrightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

The lime water looks turbid as insoluble $\text{CaCO}_3$ is produced at this stage. This turbid lime water again turns opaque when extra $\text{CO}_2$ is channeled in. At this stage $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ undergo a reaction with $\text{CaCO}_3$ and produce soluble calcium bicarbonate [$\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2$] which makes the water look opaque.
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2$$

The metallic carbonates undergo the similar kind of reactions with dilute sulfuric acid or dilute nitric acid and produce sulfate or nitrate salts.
$$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HNO}_3 \longrightarrow \text{Ca(NO}_3)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$
